verses.1: Remember, O LORD, what has happened to us. Look and see our humiliation.
verses.2: Our inheritance has been given to strangers, our homes to foreigners.
verses.3: We have become orphans with no father, our mothers like widows.
verses.4: We drank water for silver, firewood was bought at a price.
verses.5: We were chased with a yoke on our necks, we toiled, yet found no rest.
verses.6: Egypt gave its hand, Assyria brought us bread in full measure.
verses.7: Our fathers sinned, and they are no more; we have borne their sins.
verses.8: Slaves have ruled over us, and no one to deliver us from their grip.
verses.9: We were fed with our own lives, we were like wild beasts in the desert for our bread.
verses.10: Our skin burned like a furnace, consumed by the heat of hunger.
verses.11: Women in Zion were put to shame, virgins in the cities of Judah.
verses.12: The leaders were hanged, the faces of the elders were not honored.
verses.13: The chosen ones carried grief, and the young men fell from the tree.
verses.14: The elders sat in silence at the gates, the young men abandoned their music.
verses.15: The joy of our hearts has turned to mourning, our dancing into lament.
verses.16: The crown of our head has fallen. Oh, how we have sinned!
verses.17: Because of this our heart is faint, because of this our eyes are darkened.
verses.18: On Mount Zion, now desolate, foxes prowl through it.
verses.19: You, O LORD, will dwell forever. Your throne is eternal, generation after generation.
verses.20: Why have you forgotten us forever? Why have you abandoned us for so many days?
verses.21: Return to us, O LORD, and we will return. Renew our days as they were in times past.
verses.22: For you have utterly rejected us, you have been angry with us beyond measure.

notes:
Notes
- v. 19: The phrase “You, O LORD, will dwell forever” reflects the Hebrew לְעוֹלָם תֵּשֵׁב, where “dwell” is rendered to match the poetic tone and the context of divine permanence.
- v. 21: "Renew our days as they were in times past" translates חַדֵּשׁ יָמֵינוּ כְּקֶֽדֶם, where "renew" is chosen to reflect the idea of restoration rather than a literal "change."
- v. 22: The phrase “you have been angry with us beyond measure” reflects the Hebrew עַד־מְאֹֽד, which is idiomatic for an overwhelming or excessive level of anger.
